stages.name: Foundations
stages.goal: Both projects build, test and lint in CI. Neo4j, Redis and Service Bus run in Docker, the graph driver and schema migrations exist, and the Neo4j test harness wipes and round-trips the graph for every test.

stages.name: Domain rules
stages.goal: Every business rule is a pure, tested function (status, freshness, schedules, reply parsing, booking states, criteria filter, registration gate, alerts, templates), and the FHIR-to-graph mapper and resource store round-trip resources through Neo4j.

stages.name: Capacity loop: core and storage
stages.goal: Each port ships with its Neo4j adapter and round-trip tests: services, capacity, bookings, cases, people, criteria, registrations, flags, audit, outbox, unit of work, idempotency, tokens and credentials. Report, confirm, prompt and missed-report use cases run against the real graph; Redis and Service Bus adapters pass their contract tests.

stages.name: Capacity loop: channels, API and wall board
stages.goal: A reporter answers a text or a link and the wall board changes live. Milestone A: the board runs on real data.

stages.name: Advisor call
stages.goal: An advisor captures needs, sees filtered options with data age, records phoned and declined positions and closes the case. The shift lead chases late reporters and sets services up. Milestone B: pilot-ready (the pilot cut line).

stages.name: Booking by text and link
stages.goal: Advisors request bookings; services confirm or decline by text, link or app; timers expire silence; withdrawals and cancellations work.

stages.name: Registration and approval
stages.goal: Services are invited from the scope list, register themselves, and go live only after checks, a call-back, criteria second approval and a test prompt.

stages.name: Reporter app, PIN, push and alerts
stages.goal: Installed web app with PIN and push for reporters; COO and ICB users get chosen alerts with acknowledgement and escalation.

stages.name: Shift lead tools, clinical advice and safety
stages.goal: Suspend, remove, move, flags, audit replay, the clinical advice queue and safety concern reporting.

stages.name: Observability and support console
stages.goal: Browser and backend telemetry without personal values, friction rules, aggregates, and the consent-based support console.

stages.name: Later
stages.goal: Map and travel time, planning view, product tour and training, RDF export, the second SMS provider.

title: London clock change: local 01:00-01:59 on 2026-03-29 is not monotonic
body: On 2026-03-29, local 01:00-01:59 maps to 02:00-02:59 BST, and local 02:00 maps to the same instant as local 01:00. Wall-clock order is not monotonic across the gap. Schedule builders (D03, D04) must not place a due time inside 01:00-02:00 on that date, and must compare instants, never local times. Use london_time.london_to_utc from F06. Found by F06.

stages.name: Foundations
stages.goal: Both projects build, test and lint in CI. Neo4j, Redis and Service Bus run in Docker, the graph driver and schema migrations exist, and the Neo4j test harness wipes and round-trips the graph for every test.

stages.name: Domain rules

stages.name: Capacity loop: core and storage
stages.goal: Each port ships with its Neo4j adapter and round-trip tests: services, capacity, bookings, cases, people, criteria, registrations, flags, audit, outbox, unit of work, idempotency, tokens and credentials. stages.name: Advisor call

stages.name: Registration and approval

stages.name: Reporter app, PIN, push and alerts

stages.name: Shift lead tools, clinical advice and safety

title: Service Bus emulator image has no shell, so it cannot run its own healthcheck
body: The emulator image (servicebus-emulator:2.0.1) has no /bin/sh, bash or curl; docker exec and a shell healthcheck both fail. Its /health endpoint on port 5300 returns 200 when ready. F04 uses a probe container (servicebus-ready, the SQL image, which has bash) that polls http://servicebus-emulator:5300/health, so up --wait waits for the emulator. Use the same pattern for any service that ships without a shell. The emulator needs SQL Server 2022 (mssql/server), not Azure SQL Edge, per current MS docs.

title: Duplicate detection on inbound.replies makes a repeat send of the same id fail for 20 seconds
body: Queue inbound.replies has RequiresDuplicateDetection true with DuplicateDetectionHistoryTimeWindow PT20S. The smoke test sends message id smoke-1 each run, so a second run within 20 seconds receives nothing and fails. Wait 20 seconds, or use a unique id in tests that send to inbound.replies (the F10 harness should do this). Documented in infra/README.md.

title: docker compose restart returns before Neo4j accepts connections
body: After docker compose restart neo4j, the container is Up but its healthcheck is still starting, so an immediate cypher-shell or driver call gets connection refused. Run docker compose -f infra/docker-compose.yml up -d --wait neo4j (or poll health) before connecting. Data does persist across restart; down -v removes it.

title: Neo4j rejects a data write in the same transaction as a schema change
body: Running CREATE CONSTRAINT/INDEX and a MERGE in one managed transaction fails with Neo.ClientError.Transaction.ForbiddenDueToTransactionType (Tried to execute Write query after executing Schema modification). Do it instead: run the schema statement in its own execute_write, then the bookkeeping write in a second one. Both must be idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS, MERGE). See backend/src/diucs/adapters/outbound/graph_store/migrations.py.

stages.name: Foundations
stages.goal: Both projects build, test and lint in CI. Neo4j, Redis and Service Bus run in Docker, the graph driver and schema migrations exist, and the Neo4j test harness wipes and round-trips the graph for every test.

stages.name: Domain rules
stages.goal: Every business rule is a pure, tested function (status, freshness, schedules, reply parsing, booking states, criteria filter, registration gate, alerts, templates), and the FHIR-to-graph mapper and resource store round-trip resources through Neo4j.

stages.name: Capacity loop: core and storage
stages.goal: Each port ships with its Neo4j adapter and round-trip tests: services, capacity, bookings, cases, people, criteria, registrations, flags, audit, outbox, unit of work, idempotency, tokens and credentials. Report, confirm, prompt and missed-report use cases run against the real graph; Redis and Service Bus adapters pass their contract tests.

stages.name: Capacity loop: channels, API and wall board
stages.goal: A reporter answers a text or a link and the wall board changes live. Milestone A: the board runs on real data.

stages.name: Advisor call
stages.goal: An advisor captures needs, sees filtered options with data age, records phoned and declined positions and closes the case. The shift lead chases late reporters and sets services up. Milestone B: pilot-ready (the pilot cut line).

stages.name: Booking by text and link
stages.goal: Advisors request bookings; services confirm or decline by text, link or app; timers expire silence; withdrawals and cancellations work.

stages.name: Registration and approval
stages.goal: Services are invited from the scope list, register themselves, and go live only after checks, a call-back, criteria second approval and a test prompt.

stages.name: Reporter app, PIN, push and alerts
stages.goal: Installed web app with PIN and push for reporters; COO and ICB users get chosen alerts with acknowledgement and escalation.

stages.name: Shift lead tools, clinical advice and safety
stages.goal: Suspend, remove, move, flags, audit replay, the clinical advice queue and safety concern reporting.

stages.name: Observability and support console
stages.goal: Browser and backend telemetry without personal values, friction rules, aggregates, and the consent-based support console.

stages.name: Later
stages.goal: Map and travel time, planning view, product tour and training, RDF export, the second SMS provider.

title: SMS: a concatenated UCS-2 segment holds 67 units, so 2 segments hold 134, not 137
body: One UCS-2 message holds 70 UTF-16 code units. A concatenated UCS-2 message holds 67 per segment, so 135 characters need three segments. GSM-7 holds 160, then 153 per segment; extension characters count two; any non-GSM character (for example 'ł') makes the whole text UCS-2. Use sms_length.sms_segments, which is tested at the boundaries (134/135, 70/71, 160/161, 306/307). Do not count segments by len().

title: Text-code expiry and 30-day re-verification must compare UTC instants (DEC-044)
body: D27 identity_policy.py converts every datetime to UTC before it compares, subtracts or adds a timedelta. Same-zone London datetimes give wall-clock arithmetic, so 10 minutes or 30 days across 2026-10-25 come out an hour wrong. Also: a PIN's fifth wrong try gives outcome locked, a verified code is expired on any later entry, naive datetimes raise ValidationFailed, and a timestamp in the future fails closed. The PIN never enters the module; the caller passes a boolean. Read DEC-044 before U25, U32, P10 or I13.

title: Shared Concept and Identifier nodes: G05 must not overwrite them, and fragments need them
body: G03 (DEC-051) stores a Concept node keyed Concept|system|code with display and version on the node, and an Identifier node keyed Identifier|system|value. Two things follow for G04 and G05. (1) Across resources, the same concept can arrive with a different display or version. A MERGE that SETs display or version will overwrite the other resource's value. Write display and version only when the node has none, or refuse a change, and never move them to a relationship silently. Identifier use is on the relationship, not the node: keep it there. (2) from_graph rebuilds codings and identifiers from the Concept and Identifier nodes in the fragment, not from the relationship alone. A reader that loads only the root and its relationships gets NotFound. Load the nodes at the ends of IDENTIFIED_BY, CODE, CATEGORY and every other concept relationship. Lists of CodeableConcept carry conceptOrder: a list of one differs from a single CodeableConcept, so keep the property when writing and reading.

title: G04: backbone children and extension order must be loaded and written by G05
body: Backbone entries are child nodes keyed <parent>#<element>[index], and each child is a node in the fragment. from_graph walks the children, so a reader that loads only the root and its relationships gets NotFound (same trap as L59). Write each child with its labels, and keep the child props. Extensions are ext_<shortName> props on the root or child node, and a resource with several extensions also stores extensionOrder (a list of short names). Write and load it, or the rebuilt extension list is refused. A reference target that contains # is refused now (# separates child keys). Single and list backbone values differ: a list entry carries order, a single object does not. See DEC-052 items 2, 3 and 10. Found by G04.

title: Neo4j keeps a datetime's fixed offset: L58 was wrong about the offset
body: Probe on the harness Neo4j (G05): a datetime written with +01:00 reads back with a +01:00 fixed offset; a value written in UTC reads back as UTC. Only the text +00:00 comes back as Z, so a zero offset cannot be told apart from Z. L58 said Neo4j does not keep the offset; that holds only when the value was converted to UTC before the write. Do: write the offset-aware value; store a FHIR datetime as a Neo4j datetime only if formatting it again gives the same text (G05 refuses +00:00, .000 and partial dates). Affects G05, I03, P06, G14.

title: A copy of a node must not keep the live labels, or type queries return history
body: G05 writes each version of a resource as a copy of its nodes. If the copy keeps the live labels (HealthcareService_AvailableTime, Organization), every query that matches a label also matches old versions and counts them twice. Give copies their own labels (ResourceVersion, ResourceVersionPart) and let the reader set the root type. Test: count_nodes on the live label after an update (test_removing_one_of_two_available_times). Affects every repository that keeps history (P01 onward, G13).

title: Versioned writes: take the root write lock before reading the version
body: Optimistic versioning is safe only if the version is read after a write lock on the root node. G05 does a write (MERGE ... SET lockStamp) on the root first, then reads versionId. Two writers racing on one version then leave exactly one winner (test_two_writers_racing_on_one_version_let_exactly_one_win). A read before the lock lets both writers see version 1 and both write version 2. Do the same in every repository that checks If-Match. Affects G05 and P01 onward.
